執.meaning: A puppy finds a <part>round</part> ball and won't let go. You can tug, shake, even offer him a steak, and he just wags with pure <part>happiness</part>, jaws locked tight. Nothing will make him drop it. He's very <kanji>tenacious</kanji>.
執.on: At bedtime he drags the ball under his <sound>shee</sound>t and growls at anyone who comes near.
執.kun: He keeps hold of it at the vet's, halfway up a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, even in his dreams.

灯.meaning: On a dark <part>street</part>, a firefly gets tired of flying about, so it moves into a glass jar on top of the signpost and keeps its tiny <part>fire</part> burning all night. Moths queue up for a chat. The street now has its own <kanji>lamp</kanji>.
灯.on: A late walker stubs his <sound>toe</sound> on the post and thanks the firefly for the light.
灯.kun: The firefly giggles '<sound>Hee</sound>!' and glows a little brighter.

巡.meaning: A tortoise in a police cap trundles up and down the <part>ramp</part> outside the school, waving a sign at every car that roars into the <part>speed zone</part>. Round and round he goes, all day, at one inch an hour. He takes his <kanji>patrol</kanji> very seriously.
巡.on: He hides behind a <sound>jun</sound>iper bush to catch the speeders.
巡.kun: Each lap, he stops for a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon from a <sound>goo</sound>die bag tied to his shell.

責.meaning: The TV goes fuzzy during the big match, and the whole family turns to glare at the <part>shellfish</part> perched on the roof, chewing the <part>TV antenna</part>. It looks guilty, but it was the pigeon. The shellfish still gets all the <kanji>blame</kanji>.
責.on: Dad draws a pie chart: one thin <sound>sec</sound>tor for the pigeon, the rest for the shellfish.
責.kun: Even the red <sound>se</sound>tter barks at it, though the dog slept through the whole thing.

脈.meaning: Standing on the <part>moon</part>, an astronaut looks back at Earth through her telescope and spots a <part>river delta</part> splitting into a hundred blue threads, swelling and shrinking as the tide rolls in. 'It's alive,' she whispers. The planet has a <kanji>vein</kanji>, and it's pumping.
脈.on: Back at base, the only plant on the station is a sli<sound>my</sound> <sound>yuc</sound>ca, and even its leaves have little throbbing veins.
脈.kun: She traces the branching rivers in soy sauce across a plate of <sound>su</sound>shi, then in mud on the door of a <sound>jee</sound>p: a line.

債.meaning: At a fancy party, a guest borrows a fur coat and pins an IOU to the empty <part>coat hook</part>, promising to pay double next year. Next year he doesn't, so the host pins the <part>blame</part> on him in big red letters. That IOU is now a <kanji>bond</kanji>, and it grows every winter.
債.on: He pays it off at last in jugs of <sound>ci</sound>der, one for every year he was late.

各.meaning: At the family picnic, every cousin brings a <part>folding chair</part> and a <part>mouth</part> full of opinions, and nobody can hear a thing. Grandma bangs a spoon and sorts it out: one chair, one sandwich and one turn to talk for <kanji>each</kanji>.
各.on: The dog under the table gets a picked-clean chicken <sound>carc</sound>ass all to himself.
各.kun: Then it rains on every one of them. '<sound>Oh</sound> <sound>no</sound>, <sound>oh</sound> <sound>no</sound>!' cries each cousin in turn.

築.meaning: An old granny turns up her nose at <part>commonplace</part> bricks. She saws <part>bamboo</part> on her <part>workbench</part> and lashes it, pole by pole, round the <part>tree</part> in her garden, until her tree house pokes through the clouds. At ninety, she still loves to <kanji>build</kanji>.
築.on: Her cement is <sound>chick</sound>pea mash, and somehow it holds.
築.kun: A <sound>ki</sound>wi bird helps her weigh down the top floor with <sound>zu</sound>cchinis.
